title: Modular Architecture for High-Performance and Low Overhead Data Transfers
problem: Traditional file transfer tools suffer from resource underutilization and instability due to fixed configurations or monolithic optimization methods; adapting to changing network/system conditions is difficult.
motivation: Large-scale scientific data transfers across geographically dispersed locations require both speed and adaptability; static tuning cannot handle dynamic network conditions.
method: AutoMDT: modular data transfer architecture using deep reinforcement learning (PPO agent) to optimize concurrency levels for read, network, and write operations. Lightweight simulator enables offline training (~45 min) without impacting production networks.
key_novelty: First modular data transfer framework using RL for adaptive concurrency optimization with offline training capability via lightweight network-system simulator.
contributions: Modular architecture decoupling I/O and network tasks
PPO agent for adaptive concurrency optimization
Lightweight network-system simulator for offline training
limitations: Abstract-only; lacks details on specific baseline comparisons, dataset sizes, or network topologies tested
